rounds.text: The business is demonstrating explosive growth that significantly outpaces the sector, with compounded sales growth over 3 years at 23% and accelerating to 30% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. Profitability expansion is even more striking, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 1274% over the trailing twelve months and strong operational efficiency yielding an operating margin of 64% [E17, E20]. This top and bottom-line momentum is backed by robust fundamental returns, featuring an impressive return on equity of nearly 30% and a return on capital employed of 11.74%, both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E13]. Furthermore, the company exhibits exceptional cash generation capabilities, delivering an operating cash flow of Rs 1,734 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 1,137 Cr in March 2026, supported by an outstanding cash conversion ratio of 23.12x that ensures profits are fully backed by actual cash [E24, E25, E26]. Institutional confidence from domestic players is on the rise as domestic institutions increased their holdings to 27.08% by September 2026, and the company is expected to deliver a good upcoming quarter [E33, E49]. Conceded: the stock trades at a lofty valuation with a P/E of 86.2, a price-to-book ratio of 25.92x, and a negative DCF margin of safety [E1, E2, E36]. Conceded: debt levels are elevated with borrowings at Rs 5,623 Cr and a high debt-to-equity ratio alongside pledged promoter shares [E27, E29, E54].

The current valuation of Wework India Management Ltd is detached from fundamental intrinsic reality, trading at an aggressive P/E of 86.2x and a price-to-book multiple of 25.92x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E1, E2, E7]. A discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 290 per share against a market price of Rs 635, resulting in an alarming margin of safety of -119.0% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's price requires an unsustainable 29.0% earnings growth to justify itself, while the base case only assumes 18.0% [E37]. Balance sheet pressures compound these valuation risks significantly, highlighted by a towering debt-to-equity ratio of 16.49x where borrowings exceed net worth alongside a dismal current ratio of 0.33x [E27, E28]. Institutional conviction is actively eroding as foreign institutions cut their holdings from 21.97% to 17.44% and overall institutional money flow registers negative alongside a 35.0% promoter pledge [E31, E32, E34, E54]. Conceded: compounded profit growth reached 36% over 3 years and 1274% over the trailing twelve months, demonstrating powerful near-term earnings acceleration [E16, E17].

Conceded: the DCF model places intrinsic value at Rs 290 and the reverse DCF implies 29.0% earnings growth [E35, E37]. However, dismissing this execution ignores that profit growth over the trailing twelve months hit a staggering 1274% alongside a rules-based results score of 98 out of 100, meaning results are accelerating far beyond stale sentiment [E17, E63]. While debt and liquidity metrics look demanding, the operational engine is throwing off massive cash with a cash conversion ratio of 23.12x, generating Rs 1,734 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 1,137 Cr in free cash flow [E24, E25, E26]. Conceded: foreign institutions reduced stakes [E32], but domestic institutions stepped in to increase their holdings to 27.08% [E33]. Furthermore, the company commands an elite ROE of 29.8% and ROCE of 12.7%, vastly outperforming sector medians of 5.46% and 7.1% respectively, proving that premium multiples are underpinned by top-tier capital efficiency [E12, E13, E9, E67].

Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 1274% and the results score is 98 out of 100 [E17, E63]. However, citing high growth rates does not neutralize a severe valuation disconnect where the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 86.2x and a price-to-book ratio of 25.92x [E1, E2]. Conceded: operating and free cash flows reached Rs 1,734 Cr and Rs 1,137 Cr with strong cash conversion [E25, E26, E24]. Nevertheless, these cash flows are burdened by massive leverage, as the debt-to-equity ratio sits at an alarming 16.49x while borrowings actually increased to Rs 5,623 Cr [E27, E29]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased their holdings to 27.08% [E33]. Despite this, overall institutional money flow is flagged with a negative signal due to foreign institutions slashing their stake by 4.53 percentage points, and promoters have pledged 35.0% of their holding [E34, E32, E54]. Finally, while elite ROE and ROCE figures outperform sector medians [E13, E12, E67], the market price already demands an aggressive 29.0% earnings growth rate in the reverse DCF while leaving a massive -119.0% margin of safety [E37, E36].
